key_insight: Generative and multimodal AI can speed materials discovery, but truly novel claims must be judged against chemical plausibility, structural distinctiveness, property relevance, and experimental realisability.
engineering_relevance: For materials engineers, the paper reframes AI design as a feasibility-first, process-aware problem that must connect composition, microstructure, processing, and testing to deployable performance.
method: Introduces a materials property hierarchy from intrinsic composition-determined properties to extrinsic processing-dependent performance.
Uses an evidence-based multimodal framework to assess how different data modalities support structural, physical, and deployment novelty.
Calls for feasibility-first generative modelling and benchmarking grounded in experimentally realisable targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract argues that current evidence is concentrated in composition and idealised structure, while heterogeneous, under-represented, and weakly integrated modalities limit support for physical and deployment novelty.
watch_item: Benchmarks based mainly on computational labels and proxy novelty criteria can overstate progress unless modality alignment and experimental validation are built in.
paper_title: Generative and multimodal AI for materials prediction and design: Progress, challenges, and perspectives
